جَرِدٌ , (K,) fem. with ة; (S, K;) and ↓ أَجْرَدُ , (S, A, K,) fem. جَرْدَآءُ; (A, K;) and ↓ جَرَدٌ , (TA, as from the K,) which last is an inf. n. used as an epithet; (TA;) (tropical:) A place (A, K) destitute of herbage: (S, A, K:) you say أَرْضٌ جَرِدَةٌ (S, K) and ↓ جَرْدَآءُ (A, K) and ↓ جَرَدِيَّةٌ , (TA,) and فَضَآءٌ ↓ أَجْرَدُ : of which last the pl. is [جُرْدٌ and] أَجَارِدُ. (S.) ―
-b2- Also, the first, (assumed tropical:) A man affected with the cutaneous eruption termed شَرًى, from having eaten locusts. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
